patient table or bed in front

answer.evidence: The main housing is drawn face-on, like a washing machine. The round bore with its ring occupies rows 15-45, the control panel sits at rows 7-11, and the base runs through rows 47-57. The top band at rows 1-6 is thin trim with a faint line at row 5. It is a cornice-like front strip, not a receding top, so it counts as a rim of about 2 rows. Only the small patient table (rows 32-38, edge line at row 39) shows a real top surface, and it is a minor part. The big housing has no horizontal surface, and the object does not look like tall wall furniture.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a large MRI/washing-machine-like prop. Measured facts: 9 visible tones per 16x16 tile, equal to the hedge (9) but below the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 14%, close to the stall's 13%, and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted (dark blue-grey beside the white/blue body) rather than sticker black. By eye, the white casing has about 3-4 steps (white, light grey-blue, mid, dark) and the blue bed has 3-4 steps. These are fewer than the 5-6 steps of the stall and well, and the large white panels are fairly smooth with little grain or speckle. The porthole has some ring and glass shading but is simple. Overall it is clean and not sticker-like, but a careful artist would see it as thinner and flatter than the richest references (stall, well), so it falls short of the standard.

Only the small patient bed protruding at rows 31-38 shows a top plane, ending in a lighter edge line at row 39 above a grey front face at rows 40-43. The pedestal below it (rows 45-57) is a plain vertical face. The large gantry has no horizontal top surface, so the object reads as front elevation.
